issue: Dictionary specifies that IIJA projects should have suffixes ('-GS', '-EC', '-LSLI', '-LSLR') added to Project ID. Observation: base-applicant.csv row 5 shows '1019084-02-GS' and fundable-ec.csv shows '1097010-01-EC', confirming suffix convention is applied. However, suffix inconsistency exists: some files show '-LSLI' (fundable-lead.csv, comprehensive-bil-list.csv) and others show '-LSLR' (fundable-lead.csv). Clarify whether both '-LSLI' and '-LSLR' are valid or if one is a typo.
suggestion: Verify whether '-LSLI' and '-LSLR' are both intentional suffixes or if one should be standardized. Dictionary shows both in rules but provides no distinction.

issue: System Population column is numeric in all files and contains realistic ranges (702 to 334,903). No anomalies detected, but some rows show 0% NA while dictionary notes this as 'Population' without explicitly requiring NOT NULL.
suggestion: No action needed; data appears clean. Consider explicitly documenting that 0% NA is expected for this required field.

issue: Dictionary maps 'Project Score' to 'Priority Points' column. Numeric ranges vary: base-applicant.csv (3-70), base-fundable.csv (5-70), comprehensive-bil-list.csv (0-73), fundable-ec.csv (5-50), fundable-gen-supp.csv (3-57), fundable-lead.csv (0-10). This wide variance across funding sources is expected but note that fundable-lead.csv has unusually low max score (10).
suggestion: No correction needed; variance reflects different funding program scoring methodologies. Document in data guide.

issue: The grepl pattern uses 'meets_affordability_criteria' but the column after clean_names() from the source would be 'meets_affordability_criteria_dac' (as seen in the base_all select and the data dictionary reference). This mismatch means the grepl will fail silently and all rows may default to 'No'.
suggestion: Change grepl('Yes', meets_affordability_criteria) to grepl('Yes', meets_affordability_criteria_dac, ignore.case=TRUE)

issue: The dictionary specifies that an empty cell under 'Meets Affordability Criteria (i.e. DAC)' should map to 'No', and 'Yes (+4 Add\'l Priority Points)' should also map to 'Yes'. The current ifelse only checks for 'Yes' substring but does not handle NA values explicitly — NA inputs to grepl return NA, not FALSE, so rows with NA DAC may produce NA instead of 'No'.
suggestion: Use ifelse(grepl('Yes', meets_affordability_criteria_dac, ignore.case=TRUE) & !is.na(meets_affordability_criteria_dac), 'Yes', 'No') or use a case_when with an explicit is.na check.

issue: The dictionary requires adding '-GS', '-EC', '-LSLI', or '-LSLR' suffixes to ALL IIJA project IDs. The script only assigns the raw dwrlf_project_number as project_id without appending these suffixes for IIJA projects in the main pipeline. The suffix appending only happens in isolated project_description case_when lines for three specific project_ids, not as a general transformation.
suggestion: Add a mutate step that appends the appropriate suffix to project_id for all IIJA projects based on their list or project_type (e.g., '-GS' for Gen Supp, '-EC' for EC, '-LSLR' for LSLR fundable list entries).

issue: For base_all rows not on the fundable list, principal_forgiveness is populated from amount_of_principal_forgiveness in the comprehensive list. The dictionary explicitly states that AMOUNT of PRINCIPAL FORGIVENESS should only be taken from Fundable Lists, not Comprehensive Lists, because not all comprehensive list projects are expecting funding.
suggestion: Remove amount_of_principal_forgiveness from the base_app/base_all select or ensure principal_forgiveness for non-fundable rows is set to NA or 'No Information' rather than pulling from the comprehensive list column.

issue: The PWSID is constructed as paste0('LA', str_sub(dwrlf_project_number, start=1, end=7)), but the dictionary says PWSID should be 'Extracted from DWRLF Project Number'. Extracting the first 7 characters may not reliably produce valid PWS IDs if the project number format varies. No validation or pattern matching is applied.
suggestion: Confirm the exact extraction logic with the source document format (e.g., verify that characters 1-7 of the DWRLF Project Number always correspond to the PWSID numeric portion) and add a regex-based extraction if needed.

issue: The EC keyword matching string 'ec_str' is referenced in the project_type case_when but is never defined within the script. If it is not defined in the broader environment, this will cause a runtime error.
suggestion: Define ec_str within the function or confirm it is reliably available in scope, listing all required EC keywords from the dictionary (cyanotoxin, dioxane, PFAS, PFOS, PFOA, THM, HAA5, manganese, Mn, etc.).

issue: The dictionary specifies that for the Base IUP, projects with 'IIJA-LSL' under the FILTER IIJA Project column are lead projects. The script checks grepl('IIJA-LSL', iija_project) which correctly catches this, but also requires checking for lead/LSL in project_description for Base Comprehensive List projects. However, the IIJA Gen Supp Comprehensive List also requires checking for 'LSLR' (not just 'lsl') in project_description for lead classification. The current regex 'lead|lsl' may miss 'LSLR' as a distinct token or misclassify unrelated text.
suggestion: Expand the lead regex to explicitly include 'LSLR' and consider using word-boundary anchors or case-insensitive matching to avoid false positives.

issue: The dictionary requires that for IIJA Gen Supp PPL projects, 'IIJA-EC' under FILTER IIJA Project maps to Emerging Contaminants. The script checks grepl('IIJA-EC', iija_project) only in the project_type case_when, but this check comes after the !is.na(project_type) check. For bil_all rows where project_type was already set (e.g., from ec_fundable or lead_fundable), this is fine, but for gen supp comprehensive list rows the iija_project column check must fire correctly. Verify that iija_project column is retained through all joins for bil_all rows.
suggestion: Confirm that the iija_project column is present in bil_comp and survives the join/select operations so the case_when logic can access it for IIJA comprehensive list rows.

issue: The dictionary states projects not on any fundable list should map to 'No', not 'No Information'. The script uses replace_na(expecting_funding, 'No') which is correct, but should be verified against the 'No Information' category defined in the dictionary for cases where funding status is truly unknown.
suggestion: Confirm that all projects in the comprehensive lists but not on fundable lists should indeed be 'No' per Louisiana-specific rules, since the dictionary also defines a 'No Information' category.

issue: For bil_all rows, principal_forgiveness is only carried from the fundable join. Non-fundable IIJA comprehensive list rows will have NA principal_forgiveness, which gets replaced with 'No Information'. This is correct per the dictionary, but the base_all path may inadvertently retain the comprehensive list's amount_of_principal_forgiveness column value before the coalesce, potentially overwriting the fundable list's cleaned value.
suggestion: Review the coalesce logic in base_all to ensure the fundable list's principal_forgiveness always takes precedence over the comprehensive list value.

issue: For the Base IUP, the dictionary says projects with 'IIJA-GS', 'IIJA-EC', 'IIJA-LSL', or 'IIJA-Combo' under FILTER IIJA Project with value 'NO' are lead or EC projects. The script checks iija_project column values but it is unclear whether the 'NO' filter logic (i.e., filtering rows where FILTER column equals 'NO' vs. the IIJA Project column) is correctly interpreted from the source table structure.
suggestion: Clarify the source table structure: verify whether 'IIJA-LSL' is a value in the iija_project column or a separate filter column, and adjust grepl logic accordingly.

issue: The dictionary defines Geographic Reference as 'No Information' for Louisiana. The script creates a community_served column (set to NA) instead of geographic_reference. The column name does not match the standardized dashboard field name.
suggestion: Rename community_served to geographic_reference to match the data dictionary field name, or confirm that community_served is an acceptable internal alias.

issue: The dictionary defines Funding Amount as 'Estimated total amount of SRF funding awarded to the project, including principal forgiveness.' It is set to NA (as character) in the script. No transformation note says it should be 'No Information' vs NA. Confirm whether downstream processes expect the string 'No Information' or NA for missing funding_amount.
suggestion: If other NA fields like project_cost and project_name use NA, ensure consistency; otherwise standardize all 'No Information' fields to use the same representation.

issue: The dictionary specifies Project Name as 'No Information' for Louisiana. The script sets project_name = as.character(NA). Confirm whether the dashboard expects the string 'No Information' or a true NA value.
suggestion: If the dashboard standardizes missing fields as the string 'No Information', change as.character(NA) to 'No Information' for project_name, project_cost, project_rank, funding_amount, and geographic_reference.

issue: The list column is retained in the final select, which is not a standardized dashboard column in the dictionary. This is likely an internal tracking column, but should be documented.
suggestion: Confirm that the list column is intentionally kept as a non-dashboard metadata column and document accordingly.

issue: Column name mismatch: base-applicant.csv has 'Meets Affordability Criteria (DAC)' which clean_names() converts to 'meets_affordability_criteria_dac', but base-fundable.csv has 'Meets Affordability Criteria' which becomes 'meets_affordability_criteria'. The disadvantaged logic uses grepl('Yes', meets_affordability_criteria) but in base_all the column from base-applicant is 'meets_affordability_criteria_dac'. The bil_all path uses 'meets_affordability_criteria'. These are different column names and the script may silently produce NAs or fail for base rows.
suggestion: Standardize the column reference after binding or rename columns before bind_rows so that a single consistent column name is used for the disadvantaged check.

issue: The data dictionary says IIJA projects should have '-GS', '-EC', '-LSLI', or '-LSLR' appended to the Project ID. However, some projects in base-applicant.csv already have these suffixes (e.g., '1019084-02-GS', '1019044-01-GS'). The script does not append suffixes to BIL IDs; instead it uses the raw dwrlf_project_number as project_id without modification. For base-applicant rows that already carry a '-GS' suffix, no further modification happens, which is correct, but for BIL comprehensive list rows the suffix is already embedded. No suffix-appending logic exists anywhere in the script, so this is consistent but should be confirmed intentional.
suggestion: Verify that all IIJA project IDs in the source CSVs already contain the correct suffix (e.g., '-GS', '-EC', '-LSLI', '-LSLR') so no programmatic appending is needed. If any IDs are missing suffixes, add logic to append them.

issue: The join between bil_comp and fundable uses both 'dwrlf_project_number' AND 'est_loan_amount'. In bil_comp, est_loan_amount is read as character and then cleaned with clean_numeric_string (e.g., '$1,400,000.00' becomes '1400000'). In fundable-ec.csv and fundable-gen-supp.csv, Est. Loan Amount is already numeric (no '$' or commas), so after clean_numeric_string it remains a plain number string. However fundable-lead.csv also has numeric Est. Loan Amount. New Orleans (1071009-02-LSLR) has TWO rows with different loan amounts (47397000 and 38603000). The comprehensive list may only have one of these values, causing the join to match only one row and drop the other, or producing duplicates.
suggestion: Check whether the comprehensive BIL list contains both New Orleans LSLR rows. If not, joining on est_loan_amount will cause one row to be lost. Consider joining only on dwrlf_project_number and handling multi-row cases explicitly, or accept that duplicate PWSID rows are intentional.

issue: In base-fundable.csv the column 'ARPA-WSP Match Project? NO or WSP FILTER' contains values like 'NO', 'IIJA-GS', 'IIJA-LSLI' and appears to be the IIJA Project indicator, while the column labeled 'IIJA Project' contains values 'B', 'C', 'A' (water system grades). The columns appear swapped relative to base-applicant.csv. After clean_names(), the script selects 'iija_project' from base_all, which would pick up the grade values ('A','B','C') instead of the IIJA type values, breaking project_type classification for base fundable rows.
suggestion: Inspect the raw base-fundable.csv headers carefully. Rename or reorder columns before clean_names() so that 'iija_project' correctly maps to the IIJA project type field (e.g., 'NO', 'IIJA-GS', 'IIJA-LSLI') rather than the water system grade.

issue: The project_type case_when checks grepl('IIJA-LSL', iija_project) for Lead classification. In comprehensive-bil-list.csv the IIJA Project column contains 'IIJA-LSLI' and 'IIJA-LSL' as distinct values. 'IIJA-LSLI' (inventory) would match grepl('IIJA-LSL', ...) and be classified as Lead, which may be correct, but it would also match before any EC check. More critically, 'IIJA-LSL' entries that are inventory-only (LSLI) should potentially be distinguished from LSLR. The data dictionary treats both as Lead, so this may be acceptable, but needs confirmation.
suggestion: Confirm with data dictionary that IIJA-LSLI should be classified as Lead. If so, document this explicitly in code comments. If LSLI needs separate handling, adjust the grepl pattern.

issue: Atlanta Water System (1127001-02) has project description: 'LOAN TERM = 10 YEARS (100% PF since IIJA-EC)'. The ec_str grepl check runs after the lead check. However, the description also contains no 'lead' or 'lsl' text, so it would fall to the EC check. But in base-applicant.csv the IIJA Project column value is 'NO', not 'IIJA-EC'. The description contains 'IIJA-EC' which should match the ec_str pattern. This is a Consolidation Initiative project being categorized as EC due to description text, which may or may not be the intended classification.
suggestion: Review whether this project should be classified as EC or General. The description mentions IIJA-EC as context for PF but may not be an EC project itself. Consider adding an explicit override or checking the Potential Funding Source column.

issue: In base-applicant.csv, the DAC column contains 'Yes (+4 Add''l Priority Points)' (with doubled single-quote as CSV escape). After fread, this becomes "Yes (+4 Add'l Priority Points)". The grepl('Yes', ...) check will correctly match this. However in comprehensive-bil-list.csv one row shows 'Yes (+4 Add'l Priority Points' (missing closing parenthesis). This truncated value still starts with 'Yes' so grepl will match it correctly, but it indicates a data quality issue in the source.
suggestion: Add a data quality check/warning for malformed DAC values. The grepl logic is robust enough to handle this, but log unexpected values for review.

issue: In base_all, principal_forgiveness comes from base-fundable.csv via left_join. For rows NOT in the fundable list, principal_forgiveness will be NA and replaced with 'No Information'. However, base-applicant.csv also has an 'Amount of Principal Forgiveness' column that is selected as 'amount_of_principal_forgiveness' in base_all. The script does not use this column to populate principal_forgiveness for non-fundable rows, even though the data dictionary says to only use PF from fundable lists. This is intentional per the data dictionary but means the amount_of_principal_forgiveness column from base-applicant is selected but ultimately unused for PF output.
suggestion: This is consistent with the data dictionary. Add a comment clarifying that amount_of_principal_forgiveness from comprehensive/applicant lists is intentionally not used for the principal_forgiveness output field.

issue: The script creates PWSID as paste0('LA', str_sub(dwrlf_project_number, start=1, end=7)). For project numbers like '1085036-04', the first 7 characters are '1085036', giving 'LA1085036'. For project numbers like '1019084-02-GS', the first 7 characters are '1019084', giving 'LA1019084'. This appears correct for 7-digit system IDs. However, if any DWRLF Project Number has a different format or leading characters, str_sub could extract incorrect digits.
suggestion: Verify all DWRLF Project Numbers follow the consistent 7-digit prefix format. Consider using a regex extract (e.g., str_extract(dwrlf_project_number, '^\d{7}')) for robustness instead of positional str_sub.

issue: Southwest Ouachita WWKS (1073047-02-GS) has a description mentioning 'brass containing lead shall be replaced' and 'reducing DBPs'. The grepl('lead|lsl', project_description, ignore.case=TRUE) check would match 'lead' in 'brass containing lead shall be replaced', incorrectly classifying this General/GS project as Lead instead of General.
suggestion: This project is on the GS fundable list with IIJA-GS type. Since project_type from fundable already sets it (if project_type column exists), check whether the case_when correctly prioritizes the pre-set project_type. The script checks !is.na(project_type) first, so if fundable sets project_type it should be preserved. Confirm that gs_fundable does not pre-set a project_type value (it does not in the script), meaning this project would fall through to the grepl checks and be misclassified as Lead.

issue: River Road Water Works (1083008-01) description contains 'DBP remediation'. The ec_str pattern includes 'DBP', so this project would be classified as Emerging Contaminants. However, its Potential Funding Source is 'BASE / ARP?' and IIJA Project is 'NO', suggesting it may be intended as a General project with a DBP compliance issue.
suggestion: Verify with data dictionary or state source whether DBP remediation projects from the base list should be classified as EC. If not, consider excluding base-only projects from the EC keyword check or adding an explicit override.

issue: base-applicant.csv Est. Loan Amount has mixed formats: some values are '$1,750,000' and at least one is '$10,000,000.00' (with decimal). The clean_numeric_string function needs to handle both formats (with and without decimal, with dollar sign and commas). This is likely handled by a standard implementation but should be confirmed.
suggestion: Ensure clean_numeric_string strips '$', commas, and trailing '.00' or decimal portions correctly for both formats present in the data.

issue: After left_join of base_app and base_fund, the script does coalesce(list.y, list.x) for the list column. list.y comes from base_fund ('SFY25 Base Fundable List') and list.x from base_app ('SFY25 Base Comprehensive List'). So fundable projects get 'SFY25 Base Fundable List' and non-fundable get 'SFY25 Base Comprehensive List'. However, base_fund also sets list='SFY25 Base Fundable List' in a separate mutate. The coalesce logic appears correct but note that list.y values are only populated for matched rows.
suggestion: Logic appears correct. Confirm that the select() after the left_join properly drops list.x and list.y, retaining only the coalesced 'list' column to avoid confusion.

issue: fundable-lead.csv has 4 rows but only 3 distinct DWRLF Project Numbers. New Orleans (1071009-02-LSLR) appears twice with different loan amounts (47,397,000 and 38,603,000). The join with bil_comp on both dwrlf_project_number AND est_loan_amount means both rows need to exist in bil_comp with matching amounts. If bil_comp has only one New Orleans row, one fundable row will not match and will be lost from the final dataset, or the join will create unexpected behavior.
suggestion: Check comprehensive-bil-list.csv for both New Orleans LSLR entries. If only one exists, the join strategy of including est_loan_amount as a join key will cause data loss. Consider joining only on dwrlf_project_number for the lead fundable list.

issue: The post-processing case_when appends FT labels to project_ids '1021002-01-GS', '1073047-02-GS', and '1019044-01-GS' only when project_type == 'Lead'. If Southwest Ouachita (1073047-02-GS) is misclassified as Lead (due to 'lead' keyword in description as noted above), it would get the LSLR FT label appended. If it is correctly General, no label is appended. This creates a dependency on correct project_type classification.
suggestion: Resolve the project_type classification issue for 1073047-02-GS first. If it should be General, the FT label will not be appended, which may be correct. If Lead, verify the LSLR designation is appropriate.

issue: Date formats in the data are highly inconsistent: '9/30/2024', 'Jan-26', 'Jan - 2026', 'Jul - 2026', 'May - 2026', 'CLOSED 2/11/25', '06/27/2025', 'Oct-25', '4/11/2025', '12/19/2024', '10/21/2024'. The script drops this column (it appears in the select(-...) exclusion for bil_all), so it does not affect output, but it may cause parsing issues if any downstream process tries to interpret it.
suggestion: The column is excluded from output so no immediate fix needed. If future use is anticipated, standardize date parsing to handle all observed formats.

issue: fundable-ec.csv has 'Yes (+4 Add'l Priority Points' (missing closing parenthesis) as one of the distinct values. The grepl('Yes', ...) check handles this correctly, but it is a data quality inconsistency.
suggestion: Flag this malformed value in a data quality log but no script change needed for functional correctness.

issue: fundable-lead.csv has both 'NO' and 'No' (different capitalization) for Meets Filtration Requirements. This column is not used in the cleaning script output but indicates inconsistent data entry.
suggestion: No script change needed since this column is not used in output. Note for data quality tracking.
